one_month_reasoning: No confirmed company catalyst before Oct 31: the Q3'26 date is unannounced (Q1/Q2 were reported May 13 / Aug 12, MarketBeat est. Nov 10; I put ~15% on an in-window report, which only widens the spread). In-window events: FOMC Oct 27-28 after the Sep 16 hike to 3.75-4.00% (Fed transcript; dots show one more 2026 hike; Kalshi 2026-09-30: 65% hold / 33% hike), late-October hyperscaler earnings (capex guides, Meta Compute) which drove NBIS's -31% July, the 10y at 5.29% after a ~33bp jump in a week, and possible ATM supply (12.3M shares left at Jun-30) or new financing announcements. With no scheduled company event I stay near symmetric: median ~$229.5 (slight negative tilt for supply and rates), log-sigma 0.29 (106% annual vol / 3.5 plus a little for the 15% earnings-in-window chance).

fair_value.method: Blend of a site-by-site capacity-cohort DCF ($178/sh split-rate, $175 single-rate: contracted Microsoft/Meta/neolab flows at contract terms discounted at 7.5-10.5%, everything else at WACC 12.0-13.4%; owned vs leased cost split; 5-yr life at full refresh cost; 40%) and EV/NTM sales at Oct-2027 (4.0x ~$21.1B = $212/sh; 60%), on 380.6M diluted shares with converts as equity. Blended $198, ~15% below $232.28.

methods.name: DCF
methods.inputs: Site-by-site capacity-cohort FCFF 2027-2033 + Gordon terminal, valued at YE26 and rolled to Oct-2027; every inventory site is a slice with its own MW, timing, ownership, contract and probability (see site_coverage). Contracted: Microsoft 300 MW at Vineland at $3.48B/yr (TCV $17.4B / 5 yrs = $11.6M/MW) through 2030 plus 35% of 2031 (tranches delivered Nov-25 to Aug-26, so terms end Nov-30 to Aug-31); Meta 2025 ($2.9B, ~48 MW at $12M/MW, Dec-25 to Nov-30) pooled on the older energized fleet; Meta 2026 dedicated $12B as ~172 MW at $14M/MW for 5 yrs from early 2027 (FI-MAN2 70, FI-LPR 50, UK-HLW 22, US-BHM 30); Meta backstop up to $15B as a $14M/MW revenue floor for 5 yrs on ~214 MW of Highridge PA's first 260 MW (p 0.85); Q2-26 neolab deals (~70 MW at $22.5M/MW for ~2.5 yrs) on the late-2026 builds. Uncontracted: new cohorts at $18M/MW (25% 5-yr / 60% 3-yr / 15% on-demand terms, unsigned) then the round-3 decay path 100/82/62/50/45/42/38/33%; older 118 MW fleet at $12M/MW decaying from 2028. 5-yr refresh at full GPU cost $17.5M/MW (supervisor), resale 9% of GPU cost, relaunch $18M/MW. Costs (F2 fix): leased MW pay $3.0M/MW-yr (power + colocation + network) and $17.5M/MW IT capex only; owned MW pay $1.5M/MW-yr (power + site O&M + network) and $25M/MW (IT + $7.5M facility, 20-yr). Variable costs 33.8-34.3% of revenue (36.1% terminal) as in round 3. Expected active MW 867/1,562/2,277/2,880/3,298/3,458/3,663 (2027-33); revenue $12.3B/24.6B/36.2B/42.9B (2027-30); FCF -$8.5B/-4.5B/+2.0B/+7.7B; contracted revenue $7.2B/10.3B/9.8B/9.0B/6.2B/3.2B. Discounting: single-rate WACC 12.0% -> $184, 13.4% -> $151, 75/25 blend $175; split-rate (contracted flows at 7.5% for delivered Microsoft/Meta-2025, 8.5% for undelivered Meta-2026 dedicated/backstop, 10.5% for unrated neolab deals; everything else at WACC) $186/$154, blend $178. g 3%. Equity = EV + YE26 net cash ex-converts $0.6B + ClickHouse $3.5B - deferred-revenue unwind $4.5B, rolled 9 months, / 380.6M shares. Sensitivities (split, blend): life 4/6/7y $167/$176/$172; refresh relaunch $16M/$20M -> $131/$225; all new/refreshed cohorts at $16M -> $113; IT capex and refresh $20M/MW -> $138; owned facility $10M/MW -> $161; owned fixed cost $2.0M -> $156; no resale -> $157; Meta $/MW $12M/$16M -> $176/$181; without the F2 owned/leased fix -> $101.

inputs_detail.value: 649 MW: Vineland 300 (Microsoft); older energized fleet 166 (Mantsala 75, Kansas City 40, Longcross 16, Keflavik 10, Modi'in ~10, Woodbury ~10, Paris 5); late-2026 builds 183 (Bethune 120, Beit Shemesh 30, Masmiya 22, Tallinn 11)
inputs_detail.derivation: Inventory MW per site; Longcross from the UK 65 MW program less Harlow and ~9,000 B300; Modi'in and Woodbury are undisclosed, so I put ~10 MW each (judgment). The total matches the ~650 MW implied by the YE26 ARR guide ($7-9B / $12M/MW). The YE26 ARR check: Microsoft $3.5B + Meta-2025 $0.6B + Q2 deals $1.6B + older fleet 118 MW x $12M $1.4B + ~50 MW of new capacity live at $18M = ~$8B, so ~130 MW of the late-2026 builds is energized but not yet earning; I give those a 0.7 first-year factor.

inputs_detail.value: $17.4B TCV through 2031; $3.48B/yr on 300 MW ($11.6M/MW); full years 2027-30, 35% of 2031; AAA
inputs_detail.derivation: 6-K: tranches delivered in 2025-26, 'about $17.4 billion through 2031'. Tranches ran Nov-25 to Aug-26, so 5-yr terms end Nov-30 to Aug-31 (average ~Apr-31, so ~35% of 2031). Fixes F4 (round 3 ended it in 2030). Inventory MW conflict (300 MW Nebius PR vs 315/350 MW secondary): I take the company's 300 MW and put the secondary Phase 2 MW in the unidentified bucket rather than counting them here too. Who pays whom: Microsoft pays Nebius; Nebius pays DataOne lease rent (inside the $3.0M/MW leased cost).

inputs_detail.value: ~$2.9B over 5 yrs (Dec-25 to Nov-30), ~48 MW at $12M/MW on the older energized fleet; AA-
inputs_detail.derivation: 6-K figure $2.9B rather than the letter's ~$3B because the filing is primary. Sites undisclosed, so it is pooled pro rata across the older energized sites, not added as new MW (no double count). Probable collateral for the $775M facility.

inputs_detail.value: $12B over 5 yrs from early 2027 = ~172 MW at $14M/MW (FI-MAN2 70, FI-LPR 50, UK-HLW 22, US-BHM 30); 75% of 2027, 25% tail in 2032
inputs_detail.derivation: TCV and timing reported (6-K, Q2 letter 'on track'). $/MW is my judgment: Microsoft's GB200/GB300 deal works out at $11.6M/MW, plus ~20% for Rubin's higher capex per MW. Location split follows press (Finland, UK, US). Fixes F4: these flows now sit on 2027+ capacity, not in the legacy fleet.

inputs_detail.value: Floor of $14M/MW for 5 yrs on ~214 MW at Highridge PA (go-live 2028, p 0.85); third-party revenue above the floor at WACC
inputs_detail.derivation: The 6-K says Meta must buy unsold capacity on specified clusters for 5 yrs from deployment. Revenue therefore = max(market path, floor). The floor binds in years 4-5 (market $11.2/10.6M vs $14M). Cluster location is not disclosed; PA's 260 MW first phase (Oct-2027) is the earliest large owned block. Fixes F3.

inputs_detail.value: ~70 MW at $22.5M/MW, 2027-28 full, half of 2029; unrated; prepayments cover 50-60% of capex on ~70% of deals
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 letter: four deals >$1B each, mid-term 1-3 yrs, $20-25M/MW ACV. $4B+ / ($22.5M x 2.5 yrs) = ~70 MW, pooled pro rata on the late-2026 builds (Bethune, Beit Shemesh, Masmiya, Tallinn). Prepaid cash is already in YE26 cash and in the -$4.5B deferred-revenue unwind.

inputs_detail.input: Under-construction and pipeline schedule and probabilities
inputs_detail.value: PA 260/400/340/200 MW go-live 2028/29/30/31 (p .85/.85/.80/.70); Independence 100/200/300/300/300 in 2027-31 (p .85-.65); Birmingham 70+200 (p .85); Lappeenranta 50/100/110 in 2027-29 (p .90-.80); Bethune +120 in 2027 (p .90); AIB 65 gross/50 IT in 2028 (p .90); Madrid 18, Newport 14, UK fourth site 13 in 2027 (p .85); unidentified ~1.05 GW incl. Oklahoma 350/yr 2030-32 (p .40)
inputs_detail.derivation: Dates from the PA site page, the Independence groundbreaking PR (four buildings over 5-7 yrs), the Q1 letter (owned sites operational 2027) and the AIB 8-K. Probabilities: 0.85-0.90 for phases with land, power and construction under way within ~15 months; lower for later phases (power by early 2029 at Independence; Birmingham lawsuits); 0.40 for the ~1 GW of the 5 GW target with no named site. Base rate: CoreWeave's active MW has run well behind contracted power (round 1). Expected active MW reaches 3.66 GW by 2033 (round 3: 4.25 GW; about the same through 2030). Not-built MW also carry no capex, so value = probability x site NPV.

inputs_detail.input: Owned vs leased cost structure (F2 fix)
inputs_detail.value: Leased: $3.0M/MW-yr fixed, IT capex $17.5M/MW. Owned: $1.5M/MW-yr, capex $25M/MW incl. $7.5M facility (20-yr life)
inputs_detail.derivation: Research: power ~$0.08/kWh plus colocation ~$150/kW-month (~$2.5M/MW-yr) plus ~$0.5M network/maintenance = $3.0M. Owned MW drop the ~$1.8M colocation rent but add ~$0.3M site O&M, giving $1.5M. Round 3 charged $3.0M and $25M on every MW, counting the facility twice. Five owned sites (~3.1 GW) per the Q1 letter. The 10-12-yr leases (Harlow, AIB) are fixed costs charged whether or not GPU rents decay (F9).

H100: SemiAnalysis index fell ~50% in ~18 months after successors shipped ($6.62 2H23 -> $3.34 2Q25) then flattened at ~$2.80 (42% of launch); A100 rents at 23-39% of launch at ~6 yrs (Silicon Data $1.58, Ornn $0.93); Ornn shows old and new chips at ~equal $/PFLOP-hr, i.e. repricing with the cost of compute rather than to scrap. Nvidia's annual cadence means the next generation ships about a year after each cohort goes live.

inputs_detail.input: Economic life, refresh capex and resale
inputs_detail.value: 5 yrs; refresh at full GPU cost $17.5M/MW (70% of $25M); resale 9% of GPU cost ($1.6M/MW); relaunch $18M/MW
inputs_detail.derivation: Supervisor round-3 correction: refresh at 100% of GPU cost, not 80%. In my round-3 model that correction alone takes the DCF from $126 to $82 (-$44, larger than the supervisor's -$15-20 estimate, because terminal maintenance capex rises ~$3B/yr). 5-yr life matches Nebius's own 5-yr book life (fact-checked: 4 -> 5 from Jan-2026) and IREN 5; CoreWeave uses 6. On the new cost structure life is flat: 4/5/6/7 yrs $167/$178/$176/$172.

2026 guide $20-25B for 0.8-1.0 GW = ~$25M/MW, and payback 1y10m at $20-25M/MW ACV implies ~$19-29M/MW (supervisor round 1). Split 70/30 IT/facility as in round 3; the facility share is spent only on owned MW.

inputs_detail.value: 44% (2027), 47-48% (2028-30), ~42.5% terminal at round-2 yields; lower on aged cohorts via the fixed $3M/MW cost
inputs_detail.derivation: Q2'26 group adj. EBITDA margin 41%, AI-cloud segment 49.7%, FY26 guide ~40% (letter); fade for competition. Costs now split fixed per MW and variable so that low-yield old GPUs carry lower margins.

inputs_detail.value: 7.5% delivered IG (Microsoft AAA, Meta-2025 AA-); 8.5% undelivered IG (Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop); 10.5% unrated neolab deals
inputs_detail.derivation: Anchor: Nebius's $775M facility against an IG contract costs SOFR+2.50% = 6.37% floating (SOFR 3.87%), or ~7.5% fixed-equivalent (5y UST 5.01% + 2.50%). It covers >100% of the related capex, so lenders take nearly the whole contracted claim at that price. The rate includes Nebius operating risk. Meta's own 2031 notes (4.55% at issue; ~5.3% at today's curve) cap the pure counterparty component. +100bp for undelivered capacity: termination for missed delivery and discounted fees for late delivery. Unrated neolabs: roughly B-rated spreads (~450-550bp over the 5y), partly offset by 50-60% prepayments, giving 10.5%, between the IG rate and WACC.
Damodaran implied ERP 4.14% on 2026-09-01 (supervisor round-2 correction; replaces 4.42% Jul-2026). 5.0% kept as the conservative case with 25% weight.
1y realized vol 106% vs ~15-18% market; CoreWeave similarly volatile; correlation-adjusted beta of 1.8 (raised from 1.6 to keep cost of equity ~13% at the lower, sourced ERP).

Cost of equity 5.29% + 1.8 x 4.14% = 12.7% (14.3% at 5.0%); ~10% secured debt at ~5.5% after tax. Used for all uncontracted, post-contract, pipeline and terminal flows (10y 5.24% on Oct-1 changes it by <0.1pt; kept).
Nominal GDP-like; below 10y yield; Fed dots ~4.1% funds rate in 2027.
$15B Jan-2026 round confirmed in the Q2 letter; the stake is only described as a 'significant minority' and is illiquid, so I take the supervisor's ~$3.5B instead of 28% x $15B = $4.2B.
Deferred revenue $5.98B at 6/30 and >$9B 2026 prepayments are in YE26 cash and again in future FCFF; supervisor's net-unwind correction of ~$4-5B (about -$13/sh).

Jun-30 cash $8.04B; borrowings $8.55B are almost entirely convertible notes (Jun-25 $1B, Sep-25 $3.16B, Mar-26 ~$4.3B, less ~$0.8B exchanged in Aug) so non-convert debt is ~$0.8B incl. $775M secured; H2 capex ~$14B vs H2 OCF incl. prepayments ~$5B; + ~$2.8B if remaining 12.3M ATM shares sold at ~$228.

271.86M outstanding (Jun-30) + 15.8M Aug exchange shares + 21.07M NVIDIA pre-funded warrants + ~49.6M remaining ITM convert shares (Jun-25 $51.45, Sep-25 22.8M at $138.75, Mar-26 ~23.8M at ~$180-183, net of exchange) + ~10M awards = ~368M, + 12.3M ATM shares (with proceeds in net cash). All converts treated as equity, none as debt.

methods.name: EV/sales
methods.inputs: EV/NTM sales at Oct-2027: 4.0x on NTM (Q4'27-Q3'28) revenue ~$21.1B = EV $84.4B; less Oct-27 net debt ex-converts ~$7B, plus ClickHouse $3.5B = equity $80.9B / 380.6M shares = $212. At 4.5x $240; at 3.5x $185. The site model raises NTM revenue slightly ($21.1B vs $20.8B) and lowers 2027 cash burn (-$8.5B vs -$13.7B, since leased sites carry no facility capex and the late-2026 builds are paid for in 2026), so net debt falls from ~$10B to ~$7B.

inputs_detail.derivation: Interpolated from the round-4 site DCF path (2027 $12.3B, 2028 $24.6B) with the round-3 quarterly shape (round 3: $20.8B from $11.6B/$24.4B).
CoreWeave EV ~$95B / NTM sales (StockAnalysis/multiples.vc as reconciled by supervisor), with ~110% growth and $104B backlog.

Discount to CRWV's 4.9x because by Oct-2027 NBIS NTM growth decelerates (~80-100%), 10y at 5.29% and a hiking Fed compress long-duration multiples, and base rates (CRWV -1/3 in 12m despite doubling revenue) show neocloud multiples compressing as capex and dilution rise. Lower leverage than CRWV offsets part of this.
YE26 ~$0.6B net cash minus ~75% of the round-4 2027 FCF (-$8.5B) = ~-$5.8B, rounded up to ~$7B for timing and working capital; funded via secured debt/ABS/prepayments.
Supervisor's ~$3.5B: $15B round confirmed, stake % unverified and illiquid.
As in DCF.

bear.story: 2027 supply glut (Meta Compute, hyperscaler builds, CoreWeave's $35-39B capex) pushes new-deal and refresh yields toward ~$16M/MW or below (my DCF with all new and refreshed cohorts at $16M: $113) and deployment slips well behind the PA/Independence schedules; more ATM/convert issuance at lower prices on a ~380M+ base; 10y >5% and a hiking Fed compress the sector to ~2.5-3x NTM sales. Resale of retired GPUs collapses in a correlated refresh wave (no resale: -$21 on the DCF). Matches NBIS's own -47% (Oct-Dec 2025) and -51% (Jun-Jul 2026) drawdowns. The floor in this case: ~$13B of IG contracted cash flows (Microsoft to 2031, Meta to 2032, the Meta backstop) are worth ~$30/sh net of build capex and do not depend on the glut.

base.story: YE26 ARR ~$8B; Meta Rubin tranches and Highridge PA's first 260 MW arrive on time in 2027-28; exit-2027 ARR ~$18-20B; owned campuses give a structurally lower cost per MW than leased neocloud capacity; dilution continues modestly; multiple compresses from ~5x toward ~4x NTM sales as growth decelerates, roughly offsetting growth. The stock ends a little below today.

bull.story: >1GW/yr deployed on schedule at $20-25M/MW (PA 1 GW by Nov-2029, Independence on its 5-7-yr plan); exit-2027 ARR $22B+; ClickHouse IPO; financing at SOFR+250-style asset-level rates on the >$40B IG backlog; market keeps ~5-6x NTM sales. GPU-life angle: post-contract capacity re-prices near original terms (refresh relaunch at $20M/MW gives a DCF of ~$225).

thesis_break_reason: At ~$115 the equity is ~$44B on ~380M diluted shares, below the Sep-2025 conversion price of $138.75 and near the March-2026 low ($116). That is about where my site DCF lands if new and refreshed cohorts re-price to ~$16M/MW ($113), or if IT capex runs at $20M/MW with refresh at the same cost ($138), with the IG contracted book (~$30/sh) intact. Trading there would most likely mean new-deal $/MW has rolled back toward the old fleet base, the owned campuses (PA/Independence) have slipped badly, or asset-level financing has closed, rather than 100%-vol noise. Raised from $110 to the supervisor's $115 because the contracted floor and owned-site economics now carry more of the value.

Microsoft/Meta/Alphabet/Amazon Q3 earnings - AI capex guides, Meta Compute
Nebius Q3'26 results; likely first formal 2027 guidance (ARR, capex, MW)
YE26 ARR vs $7-9B guide; Polymarket AI-bubble-by-Dec-31 market resolves (8%)
Q4'26 results and FY27 guidance detail
800MW-1GW capacity coming online; ARR ramp evidence vs >1GW/yr plan
ATM sales / new convertible or ABS financings (dilution on a ~370-380M base)

key_uncertainties: What new and refreshed MW earn: relaunch $16M vs $20M/MW moves the split DCF $131 -> $225; all cohorts at $16M -> $113
Owned-site economics, the source of the F2 gain: facility capex $10M vs $7.5M/MW -> $161; owned fixed cost $2.0M vs $1.5M/MW-yr -> $156; without the owned/leased split the DCF is $101
Delivery of 2.4 GW of owned campuses (Highridge PA, Independence) on the company schedules; the probability-weighted PA and Independence slices are worth ~$72/sh
Meta 2026 terms: $/MW is undisclosed ($12M/$16M -> $176/$181); the backstop's cluster sites and floor price are not public
IT capex per MW as Rubin density rises ($20M/MW incl. refresh -> $138); resale of retired GPUs (none -> $157)
Funding of ~$15B/yr capex vs prepayments and asset-level debt, and dilution beyond ~380M shares
Rates (10y 5.24-5.29%, Fed hiking) and the sector multiple (CoreWeave ~4.9x NTM sales) behind the 60% EV/sales weight
reasoning: Round 4 rebuilds the DCF from the site inventory and splits the discount rate. (1) Restating round 3: my round-3 model reproduces $126 at its written inputs, and the supervisor's refresh-at-full-GPU-cost correction alone takes it to $82, not ~$108 as the supervisor estimated. (2) Site coverage: every one of the 25 inventory sites is now a slice with MW, timing, ownership, contract and probability. Microsoft runs to 2031 (6-K checked) at $11.6M/MW on Vineland's 300 MW. The $12B Meta dedicated order moves to new 2027 capacity in Finland, the UK and the US at ~$14M/MW. The up-to-$15B Meta backstop is a $14M/MW floor on ~214 MW at PA. The Q2 neolab deals sit on the late-2026 builds. Probability-weighted, the site schedule gives almost the same active MW as round 3 through 2030 (0.87/1.56/2.28/2.88 GW vs 0.86/1.59/2.36/3.00), but 3.66 GW by 2033 instead of 4.25. At the old cost structure this gives $98 single-rate. (3) The owned/leased fix (F2) is the big change: owned MW no longer pay a colocation fee on top of facility capex, and leased MW no longer pay facility capex on top of rent. That gives $175 (+$77), because ~70% of expected MW sits on the five owned sites. This is the assumption I am least sure of, so I show $156-161 for heavier owned costs. (4) Split rate: contracted flows net of their build capex are worth $11.5B at 7.5-10.5% vs $10.3B at WACC. They are short (mostly 2027-31) and partly offset by Meta build capex, so the split adds only +$3 (DCF $178). Life is now second order (4-7 yrs: $167-178). EV/sales rises to $212 on slightly higher NTM revenue and lower 2027 burn. Blended FV $198 (from $171; ~$164 after the supervisor's restatement). Ladder: I move the scenarios part of the way (bear $110 / base $225 / bull $400; probabilities unchanged 30/45/25) and the single-lognormal median from $210 to $218. The mixed median is ~$217 and P(>=spot) 0.463 (from 0.438). This is less than the +16% fair-value change, because the gain rests on cost assumptions (owned-site costs, Rubin capex) that the market cannot yet see in reported margins. Base rates unchanged: two ~50% drawdowns in 12 months, weak forward returns for extreme-volatility stocks, and CoreWeave de-rating while doubling revenue. The 1-month ladder is unchanged: no new in-window event, and the DCF does not move a one-month view. Research this round: 2 data pulls (NY Fed SOFR, Treasury curve) and 2 primary-source fetches (Microsoft 6-K, $775M facility PR); everything else is from the inventory's cited primary sources. FRED did not respond. No option data or priors used.

gpu_life.revenue_decay_path: Contracted capacity (85% of each cohort: 25% on 5-yr, 60% on 1-3-yr terms) at $18M/MW for the term; after the contract ends and for on-demand capacity, revenue per MW is 100/82/62/50/45/42/38/33% of launch at ages 0-7 (about -50% within ~2 yrs of the next generation shipping, then flat). Cohort yield $18.0/17.5/17.0/11.2/10.6M/MW at ages 0-4. Tail stays above the $3M/MW power+colo floor through year 7 (~$5.9M). Contract terms now by site: Microsoft $11.6M/MW to 2030 plus 35% of 2031 (Vineland), Meta-2025 $12M/MW to Nov-2030, Meta-2026 $14M/MW for 5 yrs from 2027, Meta backstop floor $14M/MW for 5 yrs on PA, Q2 neolab deals $22.5M/MW for ~2.5 yrs; older 118 MW fleet at $12M decaying from 2028.
gpu_life.note: Same approach as round 3 (contract price for the term, then the 100/82/62/50/45/42/38/33% re-lease path, refresh at the end of life), with the supervisor's correction: refresh at full GPU cost $17.5M/MW, relaunch $18M/MW, resale 9% of GPU cost. That correction alone cuts my round-3 model from $126 to $82. On the round-4 site model (split rate) lives of 4/5/6/7 yrs give $167/$178/$176/$172, so value is flat at 5-6 yrs. Holding GPUs longer now costs less, because owned MW carry only $1.5M/MW-yr of fixed cost. Company lives (fact-checked): Nebius 5, IREN 5, CoreWeave 6. Resale is worth ~$21/sh (none -> $157); I haircut it in the bear case. Key swing: relaunch price $16M/$20M -> $131/$225.

discounting.contracted_rate: 7.5% (delivered IG: Microsoft AAA, Meta-2025 AA-); 8.5% (undelivered IG: Meta-2026 dedicated and backstop floor); 10.5% (unrated Q2-26 neolab deals)
discounting.uncontracted_rate: WACC 12.0% (ERP 4.14%) / 13.4% (ERP 5.0%), 75/25 blend; also post-contract, pipeline and terminal
discounting.basis: The anchor is Nebius's own secured cost against an IG contract: the $775M facility at SOFR+2.50% (6.37% floating at SOFR 3.87%; ~7.5% fixed-equivalent on the 5y UST at 5.01%). It covers >100% of related capex, so it prices almost the whole contracted claim, including Nebius's operating risk. Meta's 2031 notes (4.55% at issue, ~5.3% at today's curve) bound the counterparty part. Undelivered contracts carry +100bp for completion risk (termination for missed delivery, discounted fees for late delivery). Unrated neolabs get roughly B-rated spreads less a credit for 50-60% prepayments. Contracted streams are measured net of their share of opex and tax and of the build capex for contract capacity built after YE26 (Meta 2026, backstop). Refresh capex and post-contract flows are at WACC. Contracted PV (12% case) is $11.5B at contract rates vs $10.3B at WACC. Sum of site values $179 + bridge -$1 = the split DCF.
